You're too kind guys!

Nielzabub:

I've been asked about this before, but I'm not sure it'd work. The "basic human" shape is pretty simple so I'm relying on using the correct colours and accessories to make the characters recognisable. Using silver/grey only, I don't think I'd get the details well enough for Champion Bot to be obviously Legacy, or Swift Bot to be obviously Wraith. I'll certainly attempt this but not feeling terribly confident.

phantaskippy:

How much time do these take to make? Also are all the parts of unity attached?

Let's see… Raptor Bot probably took 4-5 hours. That's including remaking his head several times to get it just right, and all the assembly and embroidery. The crocheting itself didn't take very long. The prototype probably took 6 hours. A second bot I'd guess I could get done now in 3-4 hours.

I didn't keep track of Unity and Visionary, but it wouldn't have been a good indication of the "typical" time if I had. Unity has a lot of fiddly bits and I created the basic design as I made her, and Visionary has some time-consuming colour changes so both took a lot longer than I'd expect a more standard character to take. I'll take note of how long AZ's creation process is.

Everything's attached to Unity except the satchel. The shirt round her waist probably would slip off eventually if I hadn't sewed it on, and the bandanna wouldn't stay put at all. Besides, the fixed bandanna meant that I had to attach less hair, and hair takes AGES.

posts.name: Silverleaf
posts.cooked:
Nope. The way the designer describes it, it was inspired by those frozen flavoured ice treats that come in plastic joined together in strips. (You rip one off, cut the top off and push the ice up through the top so you can eat it, you know the things I mean. We call them ice pops, but you guys probably have some weird name for them). His kids used to fight over particular flavours so he made a rule that you could only take a pop that was at the end of a strip, and noticed how they'd persuade each other to take the next pop so they could have access to the one they wanted. And the game was born.

It's weasels because of a brand called Otter Pops.

You get points by defrosting the weasels. It's a bizarre little game.

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
I drew a lot while I was in school, all the way to about 8th grade.  Used to get books on how to draw and practice all the time, still draw like crap, anything much past stick figures starts to get ugly.  I can't draw straight lines without an aid, but I did learn to trace well, used to do comics of my own where I'd trace the characters into new situations.  They looked good, and I learned I was much better at the story side than the art.  I stopped drawing and started writing, then turned from writing to RPG's, because there is nothing better than other people telling you a story that you wrote.  I've written my own world, and a decent number of campaigns, sadly my groups tend to break up before I get to do too much.

I know practice is huge, talent isn't anything without work, but you have to have the talent to start with.  A lot of insanely talented people never reach the top because they go so long before they ever have to really work hard at it, and lesser talents surpass them because they know how to work at it.

posts.name: Silverleaf
posts.cooked:
Yeah, true. If you don't have any talent at all you'll never get good, but I guess I'm saying that everyone's rubbish in the beginning and who knows if you have real talent or not if you don't nurture it?

And even if you have precisely zero talent some practice will make your ability less crappy, and that might be enough to satisfy you.

Personally, I only really draw when I feel the need for a character portrait for one of my RPG characters or an amusing little cartoon in a note to my boyfriend or something. I'm by no means brilliant, but my drawings are recognisable and with practice I could probably become at least a little bit good. My problem is, I lack the imagination necessary to create anything interesting. I have no idea how I'd practice that!

Well AZ is still waiting to be photographed due to my tweaking him some, lack of appropriate light, dog illness, and my own health problems. I'll get to him soon, hopefully...

In the meantime I'm working on Wraith. I know she'll take ages because of all the visible hair (each stand is tied in pairs so there's a lolt of work) but the thing I can't work out is her cape. It's purple with a red lining and that's the problem. When I did Visionary's cape I used a particular stitch that creates a loose flexible piece and then I steam ironed it to get it nice and flat and smooth. If I made a two-layer cape it'd iron okay but it'd be too thick and stiff to look or move right, so I'm considering cheating and using a single colour (probably red).

But that would be WRONG.

2 layers = too thick. 1 layer = wrong. Some experimentation is in order.

And in other news, I now have the appropriate yarn and embroidery thread to make Legacy and Tachyon. (Why is it that their bios state they have dark blonde and stawberry blonde hair respectively, but in the art it looks like the same colour? Not camplaining, since it makes life much easier for me...)
